text:
Scalise and House Republicans outline legislative priorities and criticize Democratic policies
House Majority Leader Steve Scalise, along with Speaker Mike Johnson, Majority Whip Tom Emmer, Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain, and Financial Services Chairman French Hill, highlighted on June 24 how House Republicans are advancing measures aimed at lowering costs for American families while criticizing Democrats for what they described as a shift toward socialism.
During his remarks in Washington, D.C., Scalise addressed recent developments in the Democratic Party. “I first want to express my condolences to Hakeem Jeffries for the devastating defeat that the voters of New York imposed upon him last night in his own backyard in Democrat primaries. You know, you could call it the Bolshevik Revolution of 2026, but the Mamdani takeover of the Democrat Party is official now. We've been talking about it for months, this move to the Marxist socialist left by the Democrat Party,” Scalise said. He continued: “They've become an unrecognizable party. You cannot recognize who the Democrats are anymore. This is surely not your father or grandfather's Democrat Party. They've fully embraced socialism.”
Scalise also discussed energy policy and its impact on fuel prices: "Our conference chair talked about it in relation to the Working Families Tax Cut. Today we look at global oil prices and they just dropped below $75 a barrel this morning. That's because of President Trump's leadership... And it's also because Republicans worked with President Trump to lower gas prices... Now that the president has an agreement, an MOU with Iran, you've seen those prices drop dramatically in the last few days." He added that recent legislation supporting domestic energy exploration was opposed by every Democrat.
On efforts to reduce costs for Americans more broadly, Scalise said: “You're going to continue to see this drumbeat of Republicans focusing on helping make life more affordable for working families on every front... We delivered for American families. We did it for energy costs. We're doing it for a number of other issues, and we're not done.” He mentioned upcoming legislative work including appropriations bills and a transportation bill moving through committee.
Scalise concluded by emphasizing Republican commitment: "We are not done working and delivering for the American people while the Democrats are fighting to see how far left to the socialist left they can go." Steve Scalise has served in Congress representing Louisiana’s 1st District since 2008 after previously serving in both chambers of Louisiana’s state legislature; he was born in New Orleans and holds a Bachelor of Science from Louisiana State University, according to his congressional office.
